data.title: ScienceDaily: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body’s calorie-burning brown fat
data.summary: Tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, activated calorie-burning brown fat in obese mice, revealing a potential metabolic effect beyond appetite suppression. data.title: ScienceDaily: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
data.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab experiments suggest the popular joint supplement may intensify an abnormal sugar-tagging process in the Alzheimer’s brain, although researchers say clinical trials are needed to determine whether it actually causes harm.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Diabetes study finds keeping blood sugar too steady may come at a price

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
data.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain

data.title: ScienceDaily: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space

data.title: ScienceDaily: Is the universe infinite? The answer gets weird fast
data.summary: Measurements of ancient light from the cosmic microwave background suggest that the universe is remarkably flat. Space could even be flat while wrapping around on itself in exotic ways.

data.summary: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has demonstrated remarkable pointing stability and given its powerful planet-imaging coronagraph its first look at the cosmos. The telescope can already stay locked on a target with precision comparable to aiming a laser at a dime from about 150 miles away. Its coronagraph also captured stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming that the instrument can produce focused images.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: NASA’s Roman telescope just opened its planet-hunting eye

data.title: ScienceDaily: Nearly 6 in 10 people with high blood pressure don’t know they have it
data.summary: Nearly 6 in 10 people with high blood pressure in a large England study had never been diagnosed or treated, and half of those already taking medication still had elevated readings. Researchers say a more proactive approach to finding and controlling hypertension could prevent thousands of heart attacks and strokes.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Nearly 6 in 10 people with high blood pressure don’t know they have it

data.title: ScienceDaily: 97-million-year-old fossils reveal the earliest known animal “GPS”
data.summary: Mysterious 97-million-year-old magnetic fossils may be the oldest evidence of an animal using Earth’s magnetic field like a built-in GPS. Their sophisticated magnetic structure could have helped an unknown ocean creature navigate thousands of kilometers with surprising precision.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: 97-million-year-old fossils reveal the earliest known animal “GPS”

data.title: ScienceDaily: The early universe wasn’t nearly as pristine as scientists thought
data.summary: JWST has revealed that galaxies were spreading carbon, oxygen, and other heavy elements through space just 500 million years after the Big Bang. The surprising discovery suggests the young universe became chemically enriched much earlier than expected, potentially erasing traces of its very first stars.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: The early universe wasn’t nearly as pristine as scientists thought

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists just pushed superconductors beyond their usual current limit
data.summary: Ultrashort electrical pulses allowed scientists to push superconductors closer than ever to the point where their electron pairs actually break apart. The method revealed hidden differences between superconducting materials and could open new ways to probe and control their quantum behavior.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists just pushed superconductors beyond their usual current limit

data.title: ScienceDaily: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit
data.summary: High-risk MDS stem cells appear to have an unexpected “energy addiction,” relying far more heavily than healthy blood-forming cells on a molecule called NAD. Disrupting this energy pathway selectively weakened the cancer-driving cells, revealing a potential new target for treatment.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit

data.title: ScienceDaily: Even one strength training session a week could make a difference
data.summary: Strength training may be one of the most powerful tools for staying independent as you age. Age related muscle loss, known as sarcopenia, can make everyday tasks harder while increasing the risk of falls, fractures, and loss of mobility. Research shows that resistance exercises such as squats, weights, resistance bands, and even body weight movements can preserve or rebuild strength, and surprisingly, even one session a week can produce meaningful benefits.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Even one strength training session a week could make a difference

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists find an “earthquake gate” as California fault stress hits a 1,000-year high
data.summary: Researchers say stress on Southern California’s San Andreas and San Jacinto faults has reached some of the highest levels seen in a 1,000-year simulation. Because both faults are highly stressed at the same time, the Cajon Pass junction may be increasingly primed for a rupture that could cross both systems, although the study does not predict when an earthquake will happen.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists find an “earthquake gate” as California fault stress hits a 1,000-year high

data.title: ScienceDaily: Weak sunlight can still damage your DNA, scientists warn
data.summary: Weak sunlight can still damage skin DNA if you spend enough time outdoors, according to a landmark Australian study. Even UV doses too low to cause visible redness triggered cellular damage that could accumulate over time and contribute to skin cancer risk.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Weak sunlight can still damage your DNA, scientists warn

data.title: ScienceDaily: Electrons slow to a crawl in a strange new quantum state
data.summary: Scientists at the University of Chicago have uncovered a surprising quantum state in the layered magnetic material Fe5GeTe2, where huge numbers of electrons move together unusually slowly while remaining quantum coherent. The behavior contradicts existing theoretical predictions about how the material’s magnetism should work and suggests scientists may need to rethink its underlying physics.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Electrons slow to a crawl in a strange new quantum state

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists may have found a “unifying theory” of chronic fatigue
data.summary: Scientists found that five seemingly unrelated conditions, including long Covid, ME/CFS, and PTSD, may disrupt many of the same biological networks involved in immunity, metabolism, and cellular energy. The findings could help explain their shared symptoms and may open the door to new blood tests and treatments.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists may have found a “unifying theory” of chronic fatigue

data.title: ScienceDaily: One tiny chemical difference between RNA and DNA may help explain how life began
data.summary: Scientists may have found a clue to one of the biggest mysteries surrounding the origin of life: how fragile RNA molecules could gather and survive before cells existed. New research shows that RNA is unusually good at assembling into tiny liquid-like droplets that concentrate molecules and can harden into protective, gel-like structures. Remarkably, much of this behavior may come down to a single oxygen-containing chemical group that RNA has but DNA lacks.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: One tiny chemical difference between RNA and DNA may help explain how life began

data.title: ScienceDaily: This protective enzyme could help stop fatty liver disease from getting worse
data.summary: Scientists have identified an enzyme that may act as a natural defense against the worsening of fatty liver disease, which affects an estimated 100 million Americans. The enzyme, called UBE2N, helps liver cells clear away damaged mitochondria and break down fat, potentially preventing the inflammation, scarring, and cell damage associated with the more dangerous condition MASH.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: This protective enzyme could help stop fatty liver disease from getting worse

data.title: ScienceDaily: ESA’s Juice just used Earth as a slingshot to Jupiter
data.summary: ESA’s Juice spacecraft raced past Earth on September 28, using our planet’s gravity to dramatically reshape its path toward Jupiter without burning much fuel. The flyby changed its direction by 20 degrees and increased its speed by 3.5 km/s, while also giving scientists a rare chance to test its instruments on Earth and the Moon.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: ESA’s Juice just used Earth as a slingshot to Jupiter

data.title: ScienceDaily: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule
data.summary: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples: a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe. Found inside tiny impact-glass particles, the nanoscale iron can preserve a stable magnetic signal, potentially acting like a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long-lost magnetic field.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule

data.title: ScienceDaily: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
data.summary: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
